title: Contention within Tracy integration has severe effects on multi-threaded performance
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.dev [456bdea954ee24e48cb562bfbf531de1cd96e371]

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev (456bdea95) - Fedora Linux 43 (Forty Three) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory

### Issue description

To put it simply, `TracyInternTable::mutex` (as seen [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/456bdea954ee24e48cb562bfbf531de1cd96e371/core/profiling/profiling.cpp#L121)) causes some severe contention in function call-heavy multi-threaded GDScript.

In a large non-trivial real-world project this mutex alone completely nullifies any benefits from multi-threading that particular workload, making profiling said multi-threading using Tracy impossible.

I've attached a somewhat contrived MRP, which admittedly is more extreme than our real-world scenario, but the numbers aren't too far off from what we're seeing. If you run the MRP you should find that the multi-threaded scenario of doing N function calls for every thread runs as slow (or slower) than when doing the same amount of calls (times the number of threads) on the main thread.

Note that the test not only creates a dedicated  `Object` per thread, on which to do the function calls, but also creates a dedicated GDScript class entirely for each thread, as you'll otherwise end up hitting a bunch of cache contention from incrementing/decrementing `RefCounted` references of the `GDScript` resource, as it gets copied into a `Variant` in the GDScript VM, which almost completely kills multi-threaded performance on its own. Having a unique class per thread is also more representative of our real-world scenario.

Here's the output I see with my AMD 9950X3D running Fedora 43, and `production=yes`:

```
1 thread: 7941 ms
32 threads: 14687 ms
Ideal scaling (assuming hyper-threading) would be 16x, but actual scaling is 0.5x
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build Godot with `target=template_release` and `profiler=tracy`.
2. Export the MRP project with said release template.
3. Run the exported executable from command-line (with `--headless`).
4. Note how the reported scaling is less than 1x.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[tracy-function-overhead.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26119699/tracy-function-overhead.zip)

---
*Disclaimer: AI tooling was utilized in the making of this MRP. Any code not physically typed out by myself has been carefully reviewed to the best of my ability.*
